evergreen_facts.text: Ville-Marie, the settlement that became Montreal, was founded in 1642 by Paul de Chomedey de Maisonneuve.
In 1535 Jacques Cartier visited Hochelaga, an Iroquoian village on the site of present-day Montreal.
Montreal hosted Expo 67, the world's fair held in Canada's centennial year.
Montreal sits on an island in the St. Lawrence River, near where the Ottawa River joins it.
Montreal takes its name from Mount Royal, the three-peaked hill at the heart of the city.
Montreal's Mount Royal Park was designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, co-designer of New York's Central Park.
Notre-Dame Basilica in Old Montreal is known for its Gothic Revival style and its richly colored interior.
Montreal's Olympic Stadium, built for the 1976 Games, has an inclined tower designed to hold up its roof.
Saint Joseph's Oratory, a domed basilica on Mount Royal in Montreal, was founded by Brother André.
At the 1976 Montreal Olympics, gymnast Nadia Comăneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic history.
The Montreal Canadiens, founded in 1909, have won the Stanley Cup more times than any other NHL team.
The Montreal International Jazz Festival, first held in 1980, fills downtown Montreal with concerts every summer.
Cirque du Soleil, founded in Quebec in 1984, has its international headquarters in Montreal.
Poutine, fries topped with cheese curds and gravy, is a Quebec dish found all over Montreal.
Montreal-style bagels are hand-rolled, boiled in honey-sweetened water and baked in wood-fired ovens.
Montreal smoked meat is cured, spiced beef brisket, piled high in sandwiches at delis like Schwartz's.
